circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: The Yas Marina Circuit on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi spans 5. 281 kilometers and was designed by Hermann Tilke to host the Formula One season finale. Since its debut in 2009, the venue has been the concluding round of the championship, representing one of four Middle Eastern Formula One circuits that also include venues in Bahrain, Qatar, and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: The Albert Park Circuit is a Melbourne street course that loops around Albert Park Lake and hosts the Formula One Australian Grand Prix each year, along with various support series and races. The track holds an FIA Grade 1 licence, confirming its status as a premier international racing venue.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, this 4. 326 km circuit was originally known as Österreichring and served as the venue for the Austrian Grand Prix throughout the 1970s and 1980s. Following modifications and a renaming, the track returned to hosting the Grand Prix in the late 1990s and early 2000s.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street course in Azerbaijan's capital that stretches 6. 003 kilometers, ranking among the longest tracks in Formula One racing. The venue first hosted an F1 event as the 2016 European Grand Prix before becoming a permanent fixture on the calendar with the Azerbaijan Grand Prix starting in 2017.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit is a 5. 412 km track that hosted the first Formula One grand prix in the Middle East and continues to serve as the venue for the annual Bahrain Grand Prix alongside various other motorsport categories. The facility, which holds a FIA Grade 1 license and features multiple circuit configurations, has also accommodated endurance racing and historically hosted V8 Supercar competitions.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya spans 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced design combining extended straights with diverse corner configurations, making it a versatile test for all aspects of racing performance. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification and accommodates 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: The Belgian Grand Prix takes place at this 7. 004 km track situated near Stavelot in Wallonia, which has been hosting Formula One racing since 1950. The circuit has maintained an unbroken presence on the F1 calendar from 1985 onwards, with only two exceptions in 2003 and 2006.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, this 4. 361-kilometre circuit hosts the Formula One Canadian Grand Prix annually. Beyond Formula One, the track has accommodated various international racing series including sportscar championships and North American open-wheel competitions over the years.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Located in Shanghai's Jiading District, the Shanghai International Circuit is a motorsport venue primarily recognized for hosting the Chinese Grand Prix, which ran annually from 2004 to 2019 before resuming in 2024. The facility also began accommodating electric racing competitions from 2024 onward.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Silverstone is an English racing venue positioned near villages in Northamptonshire that has been the traditional home of the British Grand Prix since 1948. The circuit gained historic significance by hosting the inaugural World Championship race in 1950, though it subsequently shared hosting duties with other tracks until securing permanent status in 1987. Beyond Formula One, the facility also stages the British MotoGP round.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring is a 4. 381 km permanent circuit located near Budapest, Hungary, and hosts the annual Formula One Hungarian Grand Prix. Completed in just eight months starting from October 1985, it made history in 1986 by becoming the first Formula One race held in Eastern Europe, built after a Hungarian connection led Bernie Ecclestone to choose Budapest over the originally intended Soviet location.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Located near Monza in northern Italy, the 5. 793 km Autodromo Nazionale is mainland Europe's oldest purpose-built racing circuit, having opened in 1922. It has continuously hosted the Italian Grand Prix since 1949, except during 1980 when it closed for renovation, and earns its "Temple of Speed" reputation through its extended straights and fast-flowing corners.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit is a 5. 807 km Japanese motorsport venue operated by Honda Mobilityland in Mie Prefecture, hosting major international racing events with a spectator capacity of 155,000. The track is particularly renowned for staging Formula One and Super Formula championship rounds.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course that navigates through Paradise, Nevada, running alongside the famous Las Vegas Strip portion of Las Vegas Boulevard. The layout winds past iconic entertainment venues including the MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas, making it one of Formula One's most visually distinctive urban racing venues.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Located in Mexico City, the 4. 304 km Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez honours two Mexican racing brothers who died in separate accidents. The circuit has returned as a Formula One venue since 2015, having previously hosted the Mexican Grand Prix during two earlier periods with a different track configuration, most recently in 1992, and currently operates under the Mexico City Grand Prix designation.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a specially constructed temporary street circuit in Miami Gardens that winds around Hard Rock Stadium, stretching 3. 363 miles with 19 corners and an average qualifying speed near 139 mph. Designed by specialist circuit architects, the track joined the Formula One calendar in 2022 as the venue for the Miami Grand Prix.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Monaco Grand Prix takes place on a 3. 337 km street circuit winding through the Monte Carlo and La Condamine districts, following the principality's waterfront. Though officially named the Circuit de Monaco, it is widely known as Monte Carlo since the majority of its layout occupies that neighbourhood.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Nestled in the Dutch coastal dunes 35 kilometers west of Amsterdam, this 4. 259 km circuit near Zandvoort hosted Formula One racing until its return to the calendar in 2021 with the revival of the Dutch Grand Prix. The venue will continue holding the race through 2025, after which its partnership with the sport concludes.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit is a motor racing facility situated north of Doha in Qatar, spanning 5. 419 kilometres with a prominent 1. 068-kilometre main straight.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Located in São Paulo, Brazil, Interlagos is a 4. 309 km racing facility that opened in 1940 and was later renamed in 1985 to commemorate the late Formula One driver José Carlos Pace. The track operates in a counterclockwise direction and houses additional karting facilities dedicated to another Brazilian racing legend.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street racing venue situated along the Red Sea waterfront in Saudi Arabia, hosting the Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix from 2021 onwards. The track has recently expanded its motorsport calendar to include Formula E racing as well.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through Singapore's waterfront district, incorporating sections of both the Downtown Core and Kallang planning areas in an urban street racing layout.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya spans 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced mix of long straights and diverse corner configurations, making it a comprehensive test of racing machinery. The facility holds FIA Grade 1 status and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: Located near Austin, Texas, the Circuit of the Americas is a 3. 426-mile FIA Grade 1 facility that serves as the permanent home of the Formula One United States Grand Prix. Beyond F1, the venue hosts major motorsport events across multiple series, including MotoGP, NASCAR, and the Lone Star Le Mans endurance race, establishing it as a multidisciplinary racing destination in the United States.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Thai-British driver Alexander Albon represents Thailand in Formula One, currently racing for Williams.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso currently races for Aston Martin in Formula One, where he has claimed two world championships in 2005 and 2006 with Renault and secured 32 Grand Prix victories throughout his 23-season career. Beyond the pinnacle of motorsport, Alonso has achieved remarkable success in endurance racing, winning the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship and two Le Mans 24 Hours titles with Toyota, making him the sole driver to capture both a Formula One drivers' championship and a world endurance championship.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli made his Formula One debut in 2025 and currently races for Mercedes, having already secured six Grand Prix victories in his early career.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Haas, competing at the highest level of motorsport.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian driver Gabi Bortoleto currently races in Formula One as a member of the Audi team. Known for his competitive performances in the sport, he has established himself as part of the manufacturer's driver lineup.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas currently races for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing extensive experience from his lengthy career in the sport. He achieved two consecutive runner-up finishes in the drivers' championship while with Mercedes during 2019 and 2020, and has claimed 10 Grand Prix victories throughout his 13 seasons in the series.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Colapinto is an Argentine driver currently racing in Formula One with Alpine, competing at the highest level of international motorsport.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Australian driver Jack Doohan has appeared in seven Formula One races between 2024 and 2025 while fulfilling reserve duties for Haas. Outside of his involvement in the sport's premier series, he competes in the LMP2 category of the European Le Mans Series with Nielsen Racing.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Alpine. The 2020 Italian Grand Prix victory with AlphaTauri stands as a notable achievement in his career.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Alexandre Hadjar represents France in Formula One competition, driving for Red Bull Racing. The French-Algerian driver brings dual heritage to the sport's competitive grid.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Ferrari who has achieved seven world championship titles, equalling Michael Schumacher's record. He holds multiple all-time records including the most race victories, pole positions, and podium finishes in the sport's history.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: Nicolas Hülkenberg is a German driver currently racing for Audi in Formula One. Beyond his single-seater career, he achieved success in sportscars, securing victory at the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 driving for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand driver competing in Formula One with Racing Bulls, representing his nation in the sport.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: The Monégasque driver represents Ferrari in Formula One and achieved his best championship finish of second place in 2022. Over nine seasons in the sport, Leclerc has secured nine race victories.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen is a Danish racing driver who has competed in Formula One across two separate periods, from 2014-2020 and 2022-2024. Currently, he races in the FIA World Endurance Championship for WRT as a BMW factory driver, while also competing part-time in NASCAR's Cup Series with Trackhouse Racing.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: British driver Lando Norris secured the 2025 Formula One World Drivers' Championship while racing for McLaren, adding to his record of 13 Grand Prix victories accumulated over eight seasons in the sport.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: French driver Esteban Ocon currently races for Haas in Formula One. Previously competing for Alpine, he achieved a notable victory at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Sergio "Checo" Pérez is a Mexican driver currently racing in Formula One for Cadillac. The veteran competitor finished as championship runner-up in 2023 while driving for Red Bull and has claimed six Grand Prix victories over his 15-year career in the sport.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Oscar Piastri, an Australian driver currently racing for McLaren, has claimed nine Grand Prix victories since joining the Formula One grid four years ago.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Australian driver Daniel Ricciardo competed in Formula One over 14 seasons starting in 2011, earning the nickname "the Honey Badger" during his career. He secured eight Grand Prix victories before retiring from the sport in 2024.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell currently races for Mercedes in Formula One, where he has claimed seven Grand Prix victories throughout his eight-season career in the sport.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz Vázquez de Castro currently races for Williams in Formula One, where he has secured four Grand Prix victories throughout his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American driver who currently races in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category with Proton Competition, having previously competed in IMSA's LMP2 class. He drove in Formula One during the 2023 and 2024 seasons.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian Formula One driver currently racing for Aston Martin.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda is a Japanese racing driver who held a reserve position with Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls in Formula One. He competed in the sport's top category between 2021 and 2026.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: A Dutch-Belgian driver competing for Red Bull Racing, Verstappen has secured four consecutive World Championship titles between 2021 and 2024. Across his 12 seasons in Formula One, he has accumulated 71 Grand Prix victories.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu is a Chinese racing driver who held a reserve position with Cadillac in Formula One. He competed in the sport's top category from 2022 through 2024, establishing himself as the sole Chinese driver to have participated in the championship.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: Operating from Enstone since its rebranding in 2021, Alpine has competed as Renault's works team in Formula One, promoting the French automaker's sports car marque. The team's only victory came through Esteban Ocon at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix, and it operated with Mercedes power units before Renault's departure from the sport at the conclusion of 2025.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin, a British automotive manufacturer, has competed in Formula One through multiple organizational structures, with its current racing operation functioning as AMR GP Limited under the Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team designation.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the racing arm of the Italian luxury automaker Ferrari, stands as Formula One's longest-running and most accomplished team, maintaining continuous championship participation since the sport's inception in 1950. The squad, colloquially known as "the Prancing Horse" after its iconic emblem, has established an unmatched legacy of success throughout its seven-decade history in the sport.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: Founded by NASCAR team owner Gene Haas in 2014, the American-licensed outfit entered Formula One in 2016 and competes under the TGR Haas F1 Team name. The team's leadership transitioned in early 2024 when Ayao Komatsu assumed the principal role, succeeding Guenther Steiner who had directed operations since the team's inaugural season.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: Sauber Motorsport AG was a Swiss engineering firm that competed in Formula One from 1993 until 2024, making it the fourth-longest-tenured constructor in the sport's history. Founded by Peter Sauber in 1970 as a sports car manufacturer, the outfit achieved notable success in endurance racing before transitioning to single-seater competition. Audi AG acquired the team and its operations in 2024 to establish the foundation for its own Formula One entry.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing is a British Formula One outfit headquartered at its technology facility in Woking, operating as a subsidiary within the McLaren Group corporate structure and ultimately owned by Bahraini investment firm Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has maintained a continuous presence in Formula One since 1954 as both a constructor and engine supplier, with its current team operating from Brackley under a German licence. The squad, now known as Mercedes-AMG Petronas, saw ownership restructured in 2022 when Ineos acquired an equal stake alongside the Mercedes-Benz Group and team principal Toto Wolff. The marque's racing heritage is celebrated through the iconic "Silver Arrows" designation.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor that commenced racing in 2024, operating as one of two Red Bull-owned squads alongside Red Bull Racing. Headquartered in Faenza with facilities in Milton Keynes, the team represents the second constructor within the Austrian conglomerate's F1 portfolio.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that began competition in 2024, operating as one of two teams under Red Bull GmbH's ownership alongside Red Bull Racing. Headquartered in Faenza with a secondary facility near Milton Keynes, the team represents the automotive conglomerate's second constructor in the championship.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Red Bull Racing, an Austrian-licensed team headquartered in England, has been a fixture in Formula One since 2005 under the ownership of Red Bull GmbH. The squad, which also operates the separate Racing Bulls team within the same conglomerate, was led by Christian Horner throughout its two-decade existence until his departure in 2025, with Laurent Mekies assuming the leadership role.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering stands as a British Formula One constructor founded by Frank Williams and Patrick Head in 1977, emerging from the remnants of Williams's previous failed racing venture. Operating from its Grove, Oxfordshire headquarters, the team has established itself as a significant presence in the sport's history and continues competing today.
